choices.reason: A measured close boronate analogue retained at 8.8 mL, while this candidate's center is near zero. Tests whether the model underpredicts this structural family.
Exploratory measurement of a high-center, high-coverage isoxazoline; the measured analogue is too dissimilar to establish a directional expectation.
Samples a nearly uncovered, rigid NH-containing cyclic carbamate. The measured cyclic carbamate has a different ring and substituents, so this tests transfer rather than presumed equivalence.
Tests predictions for nitro-substituted diaryl compounds at the same recorded flow and ipa_fraction as two strongly retained measured analogues; methoxy substitution may change the outcome.
The enantiomer of pending r6c52dc0783b9 provides a direct stereochemical comparison when both responses arrive; the measured ester is only a broad analogy.
Tests whether the high prediction for a thiophene-containing diol reflects its two hydroxyl groups or poor transfer from measured alcohols with different substituents.
Measures a methoxy-substituted aromatic hydroxy acid against measured hydroxy acids whose responses are substantially below this candidate's center.
Exploratory aliphatic alcohol at intermediate coverage; helps separate alcohol behavior from the aromatic alcohols represented in the labeled set.

Complements pending r2f4642870105 with a related sulfonamide at a different recorded ipa_fraction. Measured related compounds show appreciably different responses, making condition and substitution effects worth resolving.
Complements pending r9ec25c88b73e with a chlorobenzyl rather than thienyl substituent on a related cyclic amide; tests substituent transfer within the family.
A chloro analogue of pending rfc6cdebca706 at the same conditions tests whether the brominated and chlorinated lactones follow a shared prediction error.
Exploratory measurement of a high-center, two-stereocenter cyclic alcohol; the measured alcohol does not establish its retention but offers a limited polarity reference.
A nitro alcohol on thiophene broadens the pending thiophene measurements beyond the pending ester and tests whether aromatic nitro-alcohol behavior transfers.
Samples a relatively uncovered sulfonyl-containing ring with a high center prediction; exploratory because the measured sulfonyl compound has a different core.
A moderately predicted isoxazoline balances the high-center isoxazoline selection and tests how substituent changes affect transfer within the ring family.
Measures a two-stereocenter hydroxy ketone in a sparsely covered region. The measured hydroxy ketone supports only a broad functional-group comparison.

hypotheses.claim: The center model may underpredict retention for the boronate-containing ring family.
hypotheses.alternative: The tert-butyl substituent in the selected candidate changes retention enough that the measured chlorinated analogue is misleading.
hypotheses.learning_value: A close measured analogue provides a focused check on an extreme near-zero center prediction.

hypotheses.claim: The center model may overpredict retention for the selected aromatic hydroxy acid.
hypotheses.alternative: Its methoxy substitution creates substantially different retention from the measured acids.
hypotheses.learning_value: Resolves a large model-versus-analogue discrepancy in a polar, relatively well-represented functional-group family.

hypotheses.claim: The pending nitrile ester and its selected enantiomer may have meaningfully different retention despite identical nonchiral descriptors and conditions.
hypotheses.alternative: Their responses are close and the predicted center difference largely reflects model behavior rather than chiral recognition.
hypotheses.learning_value: The simultaneous pending and selected responses will directly test stereochemical transfer without attributing a direction in advance.

hypotheses.claim: The two selected isoxazolines may expose family-specific prediction errors at different predicted response levels.
hypotheses.alternative: Their differing substituents make their errors unrelated, so a shared correction would not generalize.
hypotheses.learning_value: Checks a high-coverage-gap prediction alongside a more moderate one without treating quantile width as calibrated uncertainty.

response.feedback_interpretation: Round zero has no prior batch outcomes or previous hypotheses to confirm, weaken or contradict. Viewed observed records provide measured responses but no premeasurement errors; prediction gaps and directional claims here remain untested. The 16 pending LCMD responses have not been revealed.
response.batch_rationale: The 16 selections complement the pending batch with a direct enantiomer, close structural and condition comparisons, and measurements outside its main high-coverage clusters. They also span low, moderate and high center predictions and several functional-group families. Coverage is used as a diversity signal, not as calibrated uncertainty; the choices target potential reductions in overall regression error rather than high retention itself.
